capture_engagement.description: Deprecated: use `tracking.engagement`. Whether the engagement events (sent, delivered, opened, clicked, bounced) of the email your code rendered are captured as analytics events of the recipient. Defaults to true. A send with `tracking` can't also carry this field. A project whose admin turned engagement capture off captures nothing, whatever the send says.

distinct_id.description: Distinct ID of the recipient's person. The send and its engagement events are recorded against that person. Defaults to the recipient's email address.

from.description: Sender of the email your code rendered, as `security@example.com` or `Example <security@example.com>`, on a verified domain of the project. Without it, the email goes out from the project's default sender, or from its only verified sender when it has no default.

html.description: HTML body of the email, exactly as the recipient should see it. Through this tool the whole request as JSON, html and text included, must stay under 1 MiB, and quotes and line breaks count twice. A larger email can't be sent here.

reply_to.description: Addresses replies to the email your code rendered go to.

scheduled_at.description: When to send the email, in ISO 8601 with a timezone offset, such as `2026-11-20T09:00:00Z` or `2026-11-20T10:00:00+01:00`. PostHog holds the email until then, at most 30 days after the request. A time that already passed sends it now. Leave it out or send null to send now.

sensitive.description: Mark the email as sensitive when it carries login links, reset tokens, or codes. Sensitive emails keep their links unchanged unless `tracking` turns clicks on, leave the subject off engagement events, and keep the content out of logs. Defaults to the matched template's setting, or true when no template matches. It can't be false when the matched template is sensitive.

subject.description: Subject of the email your code rendered.

template_key.description: Names an email whose content your code rendered, such as `order-shipped`, so its metrics, logs and status group under it. Letters, numbers, hyphens (-) and underscores (_) only, at most 256 characters. Send it with `subject` and `html` or `text`. PostHog sends the content as is and never stores it as a template.

text.description: Plain text body of the email. Without it, PostHog derives the text from html. Through this tool the whole request as JSON, html and text included, must stay under 1 MiB.

clicks.description: Whether the email's links go through a redirect that counts clicks. Defaults to true when the email isn't sensitive and false when it is. Needs `opens`. A link with `data-ph-no-track` keeps its own address.

engagement.description: Whether the email's engagement events (sent, delivered, opened, clicked, bounced) are captured as analytics events of the recipient. Defaults to true.

opens.description: Whether PostHog adds its open pixel to the email. Defaults to true.

tracking.description: What PostHog tracks for the email your code rendered. `true` tracks opens and clicks and captures engagement events. `false` turns off all of it, now and for any kind of tracking added later. An object sets each kind on its own, and a kind it leaves out keeps its default. Without this field, PostHog tracks opens and captures engagement events, and tracks clicks only when the email isn't sensitive (see `sensitive`). Turn on `clicks` for a sensitive email only when its links are safe to send through a redirect. A link with `data-ph-no-track` keeps its own address either way. Click tracking needs open tracking. A project whose admin turned engagement capture off captures nothing, whatever the send says. The object form needs a JSON body.
